name: Overtime

references.title: Labor Code art.87; DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.4 §C and ch.1 §A: hours beyond eight a day at 125% of the hourly rate on an ordinary day, 169% on a rest or special day, 195% on a special day that is the rest day or on a double special day, 253.5% on a double special rest day, 260% / 338% on a regular holiday (rest day), 390% / 507% on a double holiday. The first eight hours of a rest day, holiday or off day are priced once, by that day’s own line; this line prices only the hours beyond eight. Rates: a day is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract’s recorded days per year (313 when unrecorded), or the contract’s daily rate when the agreed rate unit is DAILY; an hour is that day ÷ the normal hours per day (8 when unrecorded).

name: Rest-day work

references.title: Labor Code art.93(a)–(b); DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.3 §D: work on the scheduled rest day is paid at least 130% for its first eight hours. A monthly salary already pays rest days only when its days-per-year factor is 365, so a 313 or 261 factor adds the full 130%. Rates: a day is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract’s recorded days per year (313 when unrecorded), or the contract’s daily rate when the agreed rate unit is DAILY; an hour is that day ÷ the normal hours per day (8 when unrecorded).

name: Work on an unpaid off day

references.title: DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.2 §E: on a 261 or 253 factor the salary pays 241 ordinary working days, so the week’s second non-working day (day_type OFF) is unpaid; hours worked on it are paid at 100% for the first eight. On 365/313/305 factors the day is inside the salary. Rates: a day is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract’s recorded days per year (313 when unrecorded), or the contract’s daily rate when the agreed rate unit is DAILY; an hour is that day ÷ the normal hours per day (8 when unrecorded).

name: Regular-holiday work

references.title: Labor Code art.94; DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.2 §D and ch.1 §A: work on a regular holiday is paid 200% for its first eight hours (260% on the rest day, 300% / 390% on a double holiday). Holiday pay excludes retail and service establishments regularly employing fewer than ten (entity_extension_data.retail_or_service_establishment with small_establishment), kasambahay, managerial staff and field / task workers (Omnibus Rules Book III Rule IV s.1). A monthly salary already pays the holiday, so only the excess over 100% is added; a daily-paid contract is paid the full multiple. Rates: a day is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract’s recorded days per year (313 when unrecorded), or the contract’s daily rate when the agreed rate unit is DAILY; an hour is that day ÷ the normal hours per day (8 when unrecorded).

name: Special-day work

references.title: Labor Code art.93(c) with the yearly holiday proclamation; DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.3 §D and ch.1 §A: a special (non-working) day worked is paid 130% for its first eight hours (150% on the rest day); a double special day 150% (195% on the rest day); unworked, no work no pay. A monthly salary already pays a special day when its days-per-year factor is 365, 313 or 261, and a rest day when the factor is 365, so only the excess is added; a daily-paid contract is paid the full multiple. Rates: a day is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract’s recorded days per year (313 when unrecorded), or the contract’s daily rate when the agreed rate unit is DAILY; an hour is that day ÷ the normal hours per day (8 when unrecorded).

name: Night-shift differential

references.title: Labor Code art.86; DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.5 and ch.1 §A: 10% of the hour’s own rate for each hour worked between 10:00 p.m. and 6:00 a.m. — the day’s multiple for an ordinary night hour and the overtime multiple for a night hour that is also overtime (ordinary day 125% × 110%); a night hour that is also overtime is read from the overtime’s own span, up to the hours beyond eight that OVERTIME prices; on a 0-hour rest day or holiday, whose overtime span is the whole day, those hours are taken inside the night window first. Retail and service establishments regularly employing not more than five workers are outside it (entity_extension_data.nsd_small_retail_exempt). Rates: a day is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract’s recorded days per year (313 when unrecorded), or the contract’s daily rate when the agreed rate unit is DAILY; an hour is that day ÷ the normal hours per day (8 when unrecorded).

name: Double holiday not worked

references.title: Labor Code art.94; DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.2 holiday pay §D.3: “If the employee does not work on a double regular holiday, the employer shall pay 200%” — the salary (or, daily-paid, the DAILY_HOLIDAY_PAY line) pays one of the two holidays and this line the second. A monthly salary already pays the days its factor counts, so this line pays the one holiday the salary does not; a daily-paid contract is paid every worked or paid day on its own, and the second holiday is not paid when the nearest preceding working day was an unpaid absence (Omnibus Rules Book III Rule IV ss.2, 6, 10). Rates: a day is the monthly basic × 12 ÷ the contract’s recorded days per year (313 when unrecorded), or the contract’s daily rate when the agreed rate unit is DAILY; an hour is that day ÷ the normal hours per day (8 when unrecorded).

name: Regular holiday pay (daily-paid)

references.title: Labor Code art.94; Omnibus Rules Implementing the Labor Code (https://elibrary.judiciary.gov.ph/thebookshelf/showdocs/2/85819) Book III Rule IV ss.2, 6, 10; DOLE Handbook on Workers’ Statutory Monetary Benefits 2024 ch.2: a daily-paid employee is paid 100% for an unworked regular holiday (a double holiday adds the DOUBLE_HOLIDAY_UNWORKED line), unless on leave without pay on the working day immediately before it — a rest day or non-working day in between is skipped (s.6(c)), and of two successive holidays the second is paid when the first is worked (s.10).
